questions.q: Who among the following constitute the National Development Council? 1️⃣ The Prime Minister 2️⃣ The Chairman, Finance Commission 3️⃣ Ministers of the Union Cabinet 4️⃣ Chief Ministers of the States (2013)
questions.e: The National Development Council (NDC) is composed of the Prime Minister, Union Cabinet Ministers, Chief Ministers of all States, and representatives of the Union Territories. The Chairman of the Finance Commission is not a member of the NDC.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: The Parliamentary Committee on Public Accounts 1️⃣ consists of not more than 25 Members of the Lok Sabha 2️⃣ scrutinizes appropriation and finance accounts of the Government 3️⃣ examines the report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (2013)
questions.e: The Public Accounts Committee consists of 22 members (15 from Lok Sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha), not 25. Its primary functions include auditing the government's finance accounts and examining CAG reports to ensure financial accountability.

questions.q: In the context of India, which of the following principles is/are implied institutionally in the parliamentary government? 1️⃣ Members of the Cabinet are Members of the Parliament. 2️⃣ Ministers hold the office till they enjoy confidence in the Parliament. 3️⃣ Cabinet is headed by the Head of the State. (2013)
questions.e: In the Indian parliamentary system, ministers must be members of Parliament, and the executive is responsible to the legislature, holding office only while enjoying the majority's confidence. However, the Cabinet is headed by the Prime Minister (Head of Government), not the President (Head of State).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Council of Ministers in the Centre shall be collectively responsible to the Parliament. 2️⃣ The Union Ministers shall hold the office during the pleasure of the President of India. 3️⃣ The Prime Minister shall communicate to the President about the proposals for legislation. (2013)
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible specifically to the Lok Sabha, not the entire Parliament. Statements 2 and 3 are correct as per Articles 75 and 78 respectively.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ National Development Council is an organ of the Planning Commission. 2️⃣ The Economic and Social Planning is kept in the Concurrent List in the Constitution of India. 3️⃣ The Constitution of India prescribes that Panchayats should be assigned the task of preparation of plans for economic development and social justice. (2013)
questions.e: The NDC is not an organ of the Planning Commission but a separate body for coordination. Economic planning is in the Concurrent List, and the 73rd Amendment mandates Panchayats to plan for economic development and social justice.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Chairman and the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha are not the members of that House. 2️⃣ While the nominated members of the two Houses of the Parliament have no voting right in the presidential election, they have the right to vote in the election of the Vice President. (2013)
questions.e: The Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Vice President) is not a member, but the Deputy Chairman is a member of the House. Nominated members cannot vote for the President but can vote for the Vice President.

questions.q: With reference to National Legal Services Authority, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Its objective is to provide free and competent legal services to the weaker sections of the society on the basis of equal opportunity. 2️⃣ It issues guidelines for the State Legal Services Authorities to implement the legal programmes and schemes throughout the country. (2013)
questions.e: NALSA was established to provide free legal aid to eligible weaker sections and to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen. It also coordinates and monitors the implementation of legal aid programs by State authorities.

questions.q: Under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, who shall be the authority to initiate the process for determining the nature and extent of individual or community forest rights or both? (2013)
questions.e: As per the Forest Rights Act, 2006, the Gram Sabha is the initial authority to receive, acknowledge, and process claims to determine forest rights before they are screened by sub-divisional and district committees.

questions.q: 'Economic Justice' as one of the objectives of the Indian Constitution has been provided in (2013)
o: the Fundamental Rights and the Directive Principles of State Policy
the Preamble and the Fundamental Rights
the Preamble and the Directive Principles of State Policy
questions.e: The Preamble specifically mentions "Justice, social, economic and political." The Directive Principles (Part IV) contain various provisions aimed at ensuring economic justice, such as equal pay and prevention of wealth concentration.

questions.q: According to the Constitution of India, which of the following are fundamental for the governance of the country? (2013)
questions.e: Article 37 states that the Directive Principles are fundamental in the governance of the country, and it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.

questions.q: What will follow if a Money Bill is substantially amended by the Rajya Sabha? (2013)
o: The President may call a joint sitting for passing the Bill
The Lok Sabha cannot consider the Bill further
The Lok Sabha may send the Bill to the Rajya Sabha for reconsideration
The Lok Sabha may still proceed with the Bill, accepting or not accepting the recommendations of the Rajya Sabha
questions.e: In the case of a Money Bill, the Lok Sabha has overriding authority. It can accept or reject any or all recommendations made by the Rajya Sabha.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct? (2013)
o: In India, the same person cannot be appointed as Governor for two or more States at the same time
No procedure has been laid down in the Constitution of India for the removal of a Governor from his/her post
In the case of a Union Territory having a legislative setup, the Chief Minister is appointed by the Lt. Governor on the basis of majority support
The Judges of the High Court of the States in India are appointed by the Governor of the State just as the Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President
questions.e: The Constitution does not specify the grounds or procedure for the removal of a Governor, who holds office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.q: With reference to Indian History, the Members of the Constituent Assembly from the Provinces were (2013)
o: directly elected by the people of those Provinces
elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies
selected by the Government for their expertise in constitutional matters
nominated by the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League
questions.e: The members of the Constituent Assembly were indirectly elected by the members of the Provincial Legislative Assemblies that had been established under the 1935 Act.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ An amendment to the Constitution of India can be initiated by an introduction of a bill in the Lok Sabha only. 2️⃣ If such an amendment seeks to make changes in the federal character of the Constitution, the amendment also requires to be ratified by the legislature of all the States of India. (2013)
questions.e: Statement 1 is false because a constitutional amendment can be initiated in either House. Statement 2 is false because ratification is required by only half of the state legislatures, not all.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Attorney General of India can 1️⃣ take part in the proceedings of the Lok Sabha 2️⃣ be a member of a committee of the Lok Sabha 3️⃣ speak in the Lok Sabha 4️⃣ vote in the Lok Sabha (2013)
questions.e: Under Article 88, the Attorney General has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of either House or any committee he is named in, but he does not have the right to vote.

questions.q: Which of the following bodies does not/ do not find mention in the Constitution? 1️⃣ National Development Council 2️⃣ Planning Commission 3️⃣ Zonal Councils (2013)
questions.e: All three are non-constitutional bodies. The NDC and Planning Commission were created by executive resolutions, while Zonal Councils were established by an Act of Parliament (States Reorganisation Act, 1956).

questions.q: The Parliament can make any law for whole or any part of India for implementing international treaties (2013)
o: with the consent of all the States
with the consent of the States concerned
without the consent of any State
with the consent of the majority of States
questions.e: Article 253 empowers Parliament to make laws for the whole or any part of India for implementing any treaty, agreement, or convention with any other country without requiring state consent.

questions.q: The Government enacted the Panchayat Extension to Scheduled Areas (PESA) Act in 1996. Which one of the following is not identified as its objective? (2013)
o: To free tribal people from exploitation
To create autonomous regions in tribal areas
questions.e: PESA aims at self-governance and protecting tribal rights in Scheduled Areas but does not involve the creation of "autonomous regions," which is a feature of the Sixth Schedule.

questions.q: Consider the following languages: 1️⃣ Gujarati 2️⃣ Kannada 3️⃣ Telugu. Which of the above has/have been declared as 'Classical Language/Languages' by the Government? (2014)
questions.e: Kannada and Telugu were declared classical languages. Gujarati has not been granted this status.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the largest Committee of the Parliament? (2014)
questions.e: The Estimates Committee is the largest as it consists of 30 members, all drawn from the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: The sales tax you pay while purchasing a toothpaste is a (2014)
o: tax imposed by the Central Government but collected by the State Government
tax imposed by the State Government but collected by the Central Government
tax imposed and collected by the State Government
tax imposed by the Central Government
questions.e: Sales tax (before GST) was a state subject where the state government both imposed and collected the tax on intra-state sales.

questions.q: Which one of the following Schedules of the Constitution of India contains provisions regarding anti-defection? (2014)
questions.e: The Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Amendment Act of 1985, contains the anti-defection law.

questions.q: In the Constitution of India, promotion of international peace and security is included in the (2014)
questions.e: Article 51 of the Directive Principles of State Policy mandates the State to promote international peace and security.

questions.q: Which of the following are associated with 'Planning' in India? 1️⃣ The Finance Commission 2️⃣ The National Development Council. 3️⃣ The Union Ministry of Rural Development 4️⃣ The Union Ministry of Urban Development 5️⃣ The Parliament (2014)
questions.e: Planning traditionally involved the NDC for approval and Parliament for final oversight. The Finance Commission deals with fiscal devolution, not planning directly.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the function/ functions of the Cabinet Secretariat? 1️⃣ Preparation of agenda for Cabinet Meetings 2️⃣ Secretarial assistance to Cabinet Committees 3️⃣ Allocation of financial resources to the Ministries (2014)
questions.e: The Cabinet Secretariat prepares the agenda and provides secretarial help to the Cabinet. Resource allocation is a function of the Ministry of Finance.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: A Constitutional Government is one which 1️⃣ places effective restrictions on individual liberty in the interest of State Authority 2️⃣ places effective restrictions on the Authority of the State in the interest of individual liberty (2014)
questions.e: The essence of constitutionalism is "limited government," which seeks to restrict state power to protect individual freedoms.

questions.q: Which of the following are the discretionary powers given to the Governor of a State? 1️⃣ Sending a report to the President of India for imposing the President's rule 2️⃣ Appointing the Ministers 3️⃣ Reserving certain bills passed by the State Legislature for consideration of the President of India 4️⃣ Making the rules to conduct the business of the State Government (2014)
questions.e: Reporting for President's rule and reserving bills are constitutional discretionary powers. Appointing ministers and making business rules are done on the advice of the CM/Council of Ministers.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The President shall make rules for the more convenient transaction of the business of the Government of India, and for the allocation among Ministers of the said business. 2️⃣ All executive actions of the Government of India shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the Prime Minister. (2014)
questions.e: Under Article 77, the President makes rules for business transaction, and all executive actions are taken in the name of the President, not the Prime Minister.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding a No-Confidence Motion in India: 1️⃣ There is no mention of a No-Confidence Motion in the Constitution of India. 2️⃣ A Motion of No-Confidence can be introduced in the Lok Sabha only. (2014)
questions.e: The Constitution does not explicitly mention "No-Confidence Motion" (it's in the Rules of Lok Sabha), and it can only be moved in the Lok Sabha because the Council of Ministers is responsible to it.

questions.q: The power of the Supreme Court of India to decide disputes between the Centre and the States falls under its (2014)
questions.e: Article 131 gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction over federal disputes between the Union and states or between states.

questions.q: The power to increase the number of judges in the Supreme Court of India is vested in (2014)
questions.e: Parliament has the authority to regulate and increase the number of Supreme Court judges through legislation.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Directive Principles of State Policy: 1️⃣ The Principles spell out the socio-economic democracy in the country. 2️⃣ The provisions contained in these Principles are not enforceable by any court. (2015)
questions.e: DPSPs aim to establish socio-economic justice but are non-justiciable (Article 37).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Rajya Sabha has no power either to reject or to amend a Money Bill. 2️⃣ The Rajya Sabha cannot vote on the Demands for Grants. 3️⃣ The Rajya Sabha cannot discuss the Annual Financial Statement. (2015)
questions.e: Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend Money Bills or vote on demands for grants (exclusive to Lok Sabha), but it can and does discuss the Annual Financial Statement (Budget).

questions.q: The Government of India Act of 1919 clearly defined (2015)
o: the powers of the Secretary of State for India and the Viceroy
the jurisdiction of the central and provincial governments
the separation of power between the judiciary and the legislature
questions.e: The 1919 Act introduced "Dyarchy" and demarcated central and provincial subjects.

questions.q: When a bill is referred to a joint sitting of both the Houses of the Parliament, it has to be passed by (2015)
o: three-fourths majority of members present and voting
a simple majority of members present and voting
questions.e: Under Article 108, decisions at a joint sitting are taken by a simple majority of the total number of members of both Houses present and voting.

questions.q: The Government of India has established NITI Aayog to replace the (2015)
questions.e: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Executive Power of the Union of India is vested in the Prime Minister. 2️⃣ The Prime Minister is the ex officio Chairman of the Civil Services Board. (2015)
questions.e: The Executive Power is vested in the President (Article 53). The Cabinet Secretary is the ex officio Chairman of the Civil Services Board.

questions.q: The provisions in Fifth Schedule and Sixth Schedule in the Constitution of India are made in order to (2015)
o: protect the interests of all the border States
protect the interests of Scheduled Tribes
determine the powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats
questions.e: Both schedules are designed for the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Tribes to protect their unique identity and interests.

questions.q: With reference to the Union Government, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Department of Revenue is responsible for the preparation of Union Budget that is presented to the Parliament. 2️⃣ No amount can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India without the authorization from the Parliament of India. 3️⃣ All the disbursements made from Public Account also need the authorization from the Parliament of India. (2015)
questions.e: The Department of Economic Affairs (not Revenue) prepares the Budget. Withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund require parliamentary law, but the Public Account does not require such authorization.

questions.q: Who/Which of the following is the custodian of the Constitution of India? (2015)
questions.e: The Supreme Court is the final interpreter and guardian/custodian of the Constitution through its power of judicial review.

questions.q: Which one of the following was given classical language status recently? (2015)
questions.e: Odia was the last language to be added to the classical language list (before 2024 updates).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Legislative Council of a State in India can be larger in size that half of the Legislative Assembly of that particular State. 2️⃣ The Governor of State nominates the Chairman of Legislative Council of that particular State. (2015)
questions.e: The Council size cannot exceed one-third of the Assembly. The Chairman is elected by the Council members from among themselves.

questions.q: "To uphold and protect the Sovereignty, Unity and Integrity of India" is a provision made in the (2015)
questions.e: This is specifically listed as a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(c).

questions.q: The fundamental object of Panchayati Raj system is to ensure which among the following 1️⃣ People's participation in development 2️⃣ Political accountability 3️⃣ Democratic decentralization 4️⃣ Financial mobilization (2015)
questions.e: The core objectives are deepening democracy through decentralization and ensuring grass-roots participation. Financial mobilization and accountability are means/secondary outcomes.

questions.q: The ideal of 'Welfare State' in the Indian Constitution is enshrined in its (2015)
questions.e: Part IV (DPSPs) contains provisions for social and economic welfare, characterizing India as a welfare state.

questions.q: There is a Parliamentary System of Government in India because the (2015)
o: Lok Sabha is elected directly by the people
Council of Ministers is responsible to the Lok Sabha
questions.e: Collective responsibility of the executive to the legislature is the bedrock of the parliamentary system.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ A Bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses on its prorogation. 2️⃣ A Bill pending in the Rajya Sabha, which has not been passed by the Lok Sabha, shall not lapse on dissolution of the Lok Sabha. (2016)
questions.e: Prorogation does not lapse bills; only dissolution does. A bill purely in Rajya Sabha remains alive despite Lok Sabha's dissolution.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Chief Secretary in a State is appointed by the Governor of that State. 2️⃣ The Chief Secretary in a State has a fixed tenure. (2016)
questions.e: The CM (not Governor) chooses the Chief Secretary. There is no fixed tenure for this post.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Gram Nyayalaya Act', which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ As per the Act, Gram Nyayalayas can hear only civil cases and not criminal cases. 2️⃣ The Act allows local social activists as mediators/reconciliators. (2016)
questions.e: Gram Nyayalayas have jurisdiction over both civil and criminal cases (specified in schedules). They use conciliators.

questions.q: The Parliament of India acquires the power to legislate on any item in the State List in the national interest if a resolution to that effect is passed by the (2016)
o: Lok Sabha by a simple majority of its total membership
Lok Sabha by a majority of not less than two-thirds of its total membership
Rajya Sabha by a majority of not less than two-thirds of its members present and voting
Rajya Sabha by a simple majority of its total membership
questions.e: Under Article 249, the Rajya Sabha must pass such a resolution by a 2/3rd majority of members present and voting.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The minimum age prescribed for any person to be a member of Panchayat is 25 years. 2️⃣ A Panchayat reconstituted after premature dissolution continues only for the remainder period. (2016)
questions.e: The minimum age is 21 years. If a Panchayat is dissolved early, the new one only serves the rest of the original 5-year term.

questions.q: The Montague-Chelmsford Proposals were related to (2016)
questions.e: These proposals led to the Government of India Act 1919, which introduced major constitutional changes like Dyarchy.

questions.q: Which one of the following objectives is not embodied in the Preamble to the Constitution of India? (2017)
questions.e: The Preamble promises "Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship." It mentions "Economic Justice," not "Economic Liberty."

questions.q: The mind of the makers of the Constitution of India is reflected in which of the following? (2017)
o: The Directive Principles of State Policy
questions.e: The Preamble contains the summary or essence of the Constitution and reflects the vision of its authors.

questions.q: Which of the following are envisaged by the Right against Exploitation in the Constitution of India? 1️⃣ Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour 2️⃣ Abolition of untouchability 3️⃣ Protection of the interests of minorities 4️⃣ Prohibition of employment of children in factories and mines (2017)
questions.e: Right against Exploitation comprises Articles 23 and 24 (forced labour and child labour). Untouchability is Article 17, and minority interests are Articles 29-30.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct? (2017)
o: Rights are privileges of a few citizens against the many.
Rights are claims of the State against the citizens.
Rights are privileges which are incorporated in the Constitution of a State.
Rights are claims of the citizens against the State.
questions.e: Fundamental Rights act as limitations on the power of the State and are claims that citizens can enforce against it.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are true of the Fundamental Duties of an Indian citizen? 1️⃣ A legislative process has been provided to enforce these duties. 2️⃣ They are correlative to legal duties. (2017)
questions.e: Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable and not legally enforceable by themselves. They are moral obligations, not necessarily correlative to specific legal duties.

questions.q: In the context of India, which one of the following is the correct relationship between Rights and Duties? (2017)
o: Rights, not Duties, are important for the advancement of the personality of the citizen.
Rights are personal and hence independent of society and Duties.
Duties, not Rights, are important for the stability of the State.
questions.e: Rights and duties are two sides of the same coin; one's right implies another's duty.

questions.q: Which principle among the following was added to the Directive Principles of State Policy by the 42nd Amendment to the Constitution? (2017)
o: Securing living wage and human conditions of work to workers
Right to work, education and public assistance
Equal pay for equal work for both men and women
Participation of workers in the management of industries
questions.e: Article 43A (workers' participation) was added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 2️⃣ Union Ministry of Home Affairs decides the election schedule for the conduct of both general elections and by-elections. 3️⃣ Election Commission resolves the disputes relating to splits/mergers of recognized political parties. (2017)
questions.e: The Election Commission (not Home Ministry) decides schedules. It also acts as a quasi-judicial body for party disputes.

questions.q: With reference to the Constitution of India, the Directive Principles of State Policy constitute limitations upon 1️⃣ Legislative function. 2️⃣ Executive function. (2017)
questions.e: DPSPs are instructions/goals for the state; they are not "limitations" or restrictions on power like Fundamental Rights are.

questions.q: For election to the Lok Sabha, a nomination paper can be filed by (2017)
o: A resident of the constituency from which the election is to be contested.
Any citizen of India whose name appears in the electoral roll of a constituency.
questions.e: To contest, one must be a citizen and a registered voter in any constituency in India (though residency in the specific seat isn't required).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ In the election for Lok Sabha or State Assembly, the winning candidate must get at least 50 percent of the votes polled, to be declared elected. 2️⃣ According to the provisions laid down in the Constitution of India, in Lok Sabha, the Speaker's post goes to the majority party and the Deputy Speaker's to the Opposition. (2017)
questions.e: India uses the "First Past the Post" system (highest votes win, even if below 50%). The Speaker/Deputy Speaker tradition is a convention, not a constitutional provision.

questions.q: Right to vote and to be elected in India is a (2017)
questions.e: Article 326 provides the right to vote; hence it is a constitutional right (and also a legal right via RPA).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Election Commission of India is a five-member body. (2017)
questions.e: The ECI is a three-member body (1 CEC and 2 ECs).

questions.q: Which of the following are not necessarily the consequences of the proclamation of the President's rule in a State? 1️⃣ Dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly 2️⃣ Removal of the Council of Ministers in the State 3️⃣ Dissolution of the local bodies (2017)
questions.e: While ministers are removed, the Assembly may be suspended rather than dissolved. Local bodies are unaffected by President's Rule.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a feature of Indian federalism? (2017)
o: It is the result of an agreement among the federating units.
The federating units have been given unequal representation in the Rajya Sabha.
Powers have been clearly divided between the Centre and the States.
There is an independent judiciary in India.
questions.e: Indian federalism is not a result of an agreement between states (unlike the USA); it is an "indestructible union of destructible states."

questions.q: Local self-government can be best explained as an exercise in (2017)
questions.e: Panchayati Raj is the institutionalization of democratic decentralization to empower people at the grass-roots level.

questions.q: The Parliament of India exercises control over the functions of the Council of Ministers through 1️⃣ Adjournment motion 2️⃣ Question hour 3️⃣ Supplementary questions (2017)
questions.e: All these are tools of parliamentary oversight to ensure the executive remains accountable.

questions.q: With reference to the Parliament of India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ A private member's bill is a bill presented by a Member of Parliament who is not elected but only nominated by the President of India. 2️⃣ Recently, a private member's bill has been passed in the Parliament of India for the first time in its history. (2017)
questions.e: A private member is any MP who is not a minister. Several private member bills have been passed in history (though none recently).

questions.q: The main advantage of the parliamentary form of government is that (2017)
o: The executive and legislature work independently.
It provides continuity of policy and is more efficient.
The executive remains responsible to the legislature.
The head of the government cannot be changed without election.
questions.e: Accountability of the executive to the legislature is the defining feature.

questions.q: Out of the following statements, choose the one that brings out the principle underlying the Cabinet form of Government: (2017)
o: An arrangement for minimizing the criticism against the Government whose responsibilities are complex and hard to carry out to the satisfaction of all.
A device for strengthening the hands of the head of the Government whose hold over the people is in a state of decline.
A mechanism of parliamentary democracy for ensuring collective responsibility of the Government to the people.
A mechanism for speeding up the activities of the Government whose responsibilities are increasing day by day.
questions.e: The Cabinet system ensures the government acts as a unit and remains collectively responsible to the House.

questions.q: In India, Judicial Review implies (2017)
o: The power of the Judiciary to review all the legislative enactments before they are assented to by the President.
The power of the Judiciary to review its own judgements given earlier in similar or different cases.
The power of the Judiciary to question the wisdom of the laws enacted by the Legislatures.
The power of the Judiciary to pronounce upon the constitutionality of laws and executive orders.
questions.e: Judicial review allows courts to strike down laws/orders that violate the Constitution.

questions.q: Democracy's superior virtue lies in the fact that it calls into activity (2017)
o: The methods for strengthening executive leadership.
The intelligence and character of ordinary men and women.
A band of dedicated party workers.
A superior individual with dynamism and vision.
questions.e: Democracy relies on and encourages the participation of every citizen.

questions.q: One of the implications of equality in society is the absence of (2017)
questions.e: Equality means the absence of special privileges for any section of society.

questions.q: In the federation established by the Government on India Act of 1935, Residuary Power were given to the (2018)
questions.e: Under the 1935 Act, residuary powers were neither with the federal nor provincial legislatures but vested in the Governor General.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Aadhaar card can be used as a proof of citizenship or domicile. 2️⃣ Once issued, Aadhaar number cannot be deactivated or omitted by the Issuing Authority. (2018)
questions.e: Aadhaar is proof of identity/residence, not citizenship. The authority (UIDAI) can deactivate numbers.

questions.q: Right to Privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of Right to Life and Personal Liberty. Which of the following in the Constitution of India correctly and appropriately imply the above statement? (2018)
o: Article 14 and the provisions under the 42nd Amendment to the Constitution
Article 24 and the provisions under the 44th Amendment to the Constitution
Article 17 and the Directive Principles of State Policy in Part IV
Article 21 and the freedoms guaranteed in Part III
questions.e: In the Puttaswamy case, the SC ruled privacy is protected under Article 21.

questions.q: With reference to the election of the President of India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The value of the vote of each MLA varies from State to State. 2️⃣ The value of the vote of MPs of the Lok Sabha is more than the value of the vote of MPs of the Rajya Sabha. (2018)
questions.e: MLA vote value depends on state population. All MPs (LS and RS) have the same vote value.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ No criminal proceedings shall be instituted against the Governor of a State any court during his term of office. 2️⃣ The emoluments and allowances of the Governor of a State shall not be diminished during his term of office. (2018)
questions.e: Governors enjoy constitutional immunity from criminal cases while in office, and their salary cannot be reduced to their disadvantage.

questions.q: With reference to the Parliament of India, which of the following Parliamentary Committees scrutinizes and reports to the House whether the powers to make regulations, rules, sub-rules, by-laws, etc. conferred by the Constitution or delegated by the Parliament are being properly exercised by the Executive within the scope of such delegation? (2018)
questions.e: This committee ensures that "delegated legislation" stays within its legal bounds.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly shall vacate his/her office if he/ she ceases to be a member of the Assembly. 2️⃣ Whenever the Legislative Assembly is dissolved, the Speaker shall vacate his/her office immediately. (2018)
questions.e: A member must be in the house to be Speaker. However, after dissolution, the Speaker stays in office until the first meeting of the new house.

questions.q: If the President of India exercises his power as provided under Article 356 of the Constitution in respect of a particular State, then (2018)
o: the powers of the Legislature of that State shall be exercisable by or under the authority of the Parliament.
Article 19 is suspended in that State.
the Assembly of the State is automatically dissolved.
the President can make laws relating to that State.
questions.e: Parliament takes over the legislative powers of the state during President's Rule.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Parliament of India can place a particular law in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution of India. 2️⃣ The validity of a law placed in the Ninth Schedule cannot be examined by any court and no judgement can be made on it. (2018)
questions.e: Laws in the 9th Schedule are now subject to judicial review if they violate the "basic structure" (I.R. Coelho case).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ In the first Lok Sabha, the single largest party in the opposition was the Swatantra Party. 2️⃣ In the Lok Sabha, a "Leader of the Opposition" was recognized for the first time in 1969. 3️⃣ In the Lok Sabha, if a party does not have a minimum of 75 members, its leader cannot be recognized as the Leader of the Opposition. (2018)
questions.e: CPI was the largest opposition in the 1st LS. 1969 was the first formal LoP recognition. The requirement is 10% of seats (55 members).

questions.q: Which one of the following reflects the nicest, appropriate relationship between law and liberty? (2018)
o: If laws are changed too often, liberty is in danger.
If there is liberty, laws have to be made by the people.
If there are no laws, there is no liberty.
if there are more laws, there is less liberty.
questions.e: Law protects liberty from anarchy and interference; without law, might makes right.

questions.q: Which of the following are regarded as the main features of the "Rule of Law"? 1️⃣ Limitation of powers 2️⃣ Equality before law 3️⃣ People's responsibility to the Government 4️⃣ Liberty and civil rights (2018)
questions.e: Rule of law (A.V. Dicey) emphasizes equality, limited power, and individual rights. It's the government's responsibility to the people, not vice versa.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ As per the Right to Education (RTE) Act, to be eligible for appointment as a teacher in a State, a person would be required to possess the minimum qualification laid down by the concerned State Council of Teacher Education. 2️⃣ As per the RTE Act, for teaching primary classes, a candidate is required to pass a Teacher Eligibility Test conducted in accordance with the National Council of Teacher Education guidelines. 3️⃣ In India, more than 90% of teacher education institutions are directly under the State Governments. (2018)
questions.e: NCTE (Central) sets the minimum qualifications, not the state councils. Most teacher training centers are private.

questions.q: How is the National Green Tribunal (NGT) different from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)? 1️⃣ The NGT has been established by an Act whereas the CPCB has been created by an executive order of the Government. 2️⃣ The NGT provides environmental justice and helps reduce the burden of litigation in the higher courts whereas the CPCB promotes cleanliness of streams and wells, and aims to improve the quality of air in the country. (2018)
questions.e: Both are statutory bodies (CPCB was created by the Water Act 1974, not an executive order).

questions.q: Regarding Money Bill, which of the following statement is not correct? (2018)
o: A Money Bill deals with the regulation of borrowing of money or giving of any guarantee by the Government of India.
A Money bill is concerned with the appropriation of moneys out of the Contingency Fund of India.
A bill shall be deemed to be a Money Bill if it contains only provisions relating to imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of any tax.
A Money Bill has provisions for the custody of the Consolidated Fund of India or the Contingency Fund of India.
questions.e: Money Bills deal with appropriation from the Consolidated Fund, not the Contingency Fund.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India safeguards one's right to marry the person of one's choice? (2019)
questions.e: The SC in Hadiya case affirmed this as part of the right to life and liberty.

questions.q: Under which schedule of the Constitution of India can the transfer of tribal land to private parties for mining be declared null and void? (2019)
questions.e: The 5th Schedule protects tribal land rights; Samatha vs. State of AP case affirmed this protection.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ As per recent amendment to the India Forest Act, 1927, forest dwellers have the right to fell the bamboos grown on the forest areas. 2️⃣ As per the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, bamboo is a minor forest produce. 3️⃣ The Scheduled Tribes and other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 allows ownership of minor forest produce to forest dwellers. (2019)
questions.e: Bamboo is classified as "minor forest produce" under the 2006 Act, which grants ownership to dwellers. The IFA amendment (2017) removed bamboo from the definition of "tree" for non-forest areas, not forest areas.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The 44th Amendment to the Constitution of India introduced an Article placing the election of the Prime Minister beyond judicial review. 2️⃣ The Supreme Court of India struck down the 99th Amendment to the Constitution of India as being violative of the independence of judiciary. (2019)
questions.e: The 39th Amendment (not 44th) tried to shield the PM's election. The 99th Amendment (NJAC) was indeed struck down.

questions.q: The Ninth Schedule was introduced in the Constitution of India during the prime ministership of (2019)
questions.e: It was added by the 1st Constitutional Amendment in 1951.

questions.q: With reference to the Constitution of India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ No High Court shall have the jurisdiction to declare any central law to be constitutionally invalid. 2️⃣ An amendment to the Constitution of India cannot be called into question by the Supreme Court of India. (2019)
questions.e: Both statements are false; High Courts can strike down central laws, and SC can review any amendment if it violates basic structure.

questions.q: Article 142 of the Constitution of India could mean which one of the following? (2019)
o: The decisions taken by the Election Commission of India while discharging its duties can not be challenged in any court of law.
In the event of grave financial crises in the country, the President of India can declare Financial Emergency without the counsel from the cabinet.
State Legislatures can not make laws on certain matters without the concurrence of the Union legislature.
The Supreme Court of India is not constrained in the exercise of its powers by laws made by the parliament.
questions.e: Article 142 allows the SC to do "complete justice," granting it expansive power that overrides statutory law.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The motion to impeach a judge of the Supreme Court of India cannot be rejected by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha as per the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968. 2️⃣ The constitution of India defines and gives details of what constitutes 'incapacity and proved misbehaviour' of the judges of the Supreme Court of India. 3️⃣ The details of the process of the impeachment of the judges of the Supreme Court of India are given in the judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968. 4️⃣ If the motion of the impeachment of a judge is taken up for voting, the law requires the motion to be backed by each house of the parliament and supported by a majority of total membership of that house and by not less than two-thirds of total members of that House present and voting. (2019)
questions.e: The Speaker has discretion to admit or refuse the motion. "Incapacity" is not defined in the Constitution. Statements 3 and 4 correctly describe the statutory and constitutional process.

questions.q: Which one of the following suggested that the Governor should be an eminent person from outside the State and should be a detached figure without intense political links or should not have taken part in politics in the recent past? (2019)
o: National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (2000)
questions.e: This was a major recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission to ensure the neutrality of the Governor's office.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959 exempts several posts from disqualification on the grounds of 'Office of Profit'. 2️⃣ The above-mentioned Act was amended five times. 3️⃣ The term 'Office of Profit' is well-defined in the Constitution of India. (2019)
questions.e: "Office of Profit" is not defined in the Constitution. The 1959 Act lists exceptions and has been frequently amended.

questions.q: With reference to the Legislative Assembly of a State in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Governor makes a customary address to members of the house at the commencement of the first session of the year. 2️⃣ When a State Legislature does not have a rule on the particular matter, it follows the Lok Sabha rule on that matter. (2019)
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct (Article 176). Statement 2 is incorrect as states make their own rules; they don't automatically follow LS rules.

questions.q: In the context of polity, which one of the following would you accept as the most appropriate definition of liberty? (2019)
o: Opportunity to do whatever one likes
Protection against the tyranny of political rulers
questions.e: Positive liberty is not just lack of hurdles but the presence of conditions to reach one's potential.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about 'the Charter Act of 1813': 1️⃣ It ended the trade monopoly of the East India Company in India except for trade in tea and trade with China. 2️⃣ It asserted the sovereignty of the British Crown over the Indian territories held by the Company. 3️⃣ The revenues of India were now controlled by the British Parliament. (2019)
questions.e: Statement 3 is false as Parliament did not take direct control of revenues until 1858. Statements 1 and 2 are core features of the 1813 Act.

questions.q: In India, which of the following review the independent regulators in sectors like tele communications, insurance, electricity etc.? 1️⃣ Ad Hoc Committees set up by the Parliament 2️⃣ Parliamentary Department Related Standing Committees 3️⃣ Finance Commission 4️⃣ Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission 5️⃣ NITI Aayog (2019)
questions.e: Committees of Parliament (Ad hoc and Standing) have the mandate to oversee regulator performance. NITI Aayog and Finance Commission have different roles.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) is the first regulatory body set up by the Government of India. 2️⃣ One of the tasks of PNGRB is to ensure competitive markets for gas. 3️⃣ Appeals against the decisions of PNGRB go before the Appellate Tribunals for Electricity. (2019)
questions.e: PNGRB was established in 2006, much later than regulators like RBI or SEBI. APTEL hears its appeals.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Aadhaar metadata cannot be stored for more than three months. 2️⃣ State cannot enter into any contract with private corporations for sharing of Aadhaar data. 3️⃣ Aadhaar is mandatory for obtaining insurance products. 4️⃣ Aadhaar is mandatory for getting benefits funded out of the Consolidated Fund of India. (2020)
questions.e: The SC struck down metadata storage (previously 6 months, now limited) and sharing with private firms. Aadhaar is only mandatory for govt subsidies (Article 7).

questions.q: Rajya Sabha has equal powers with Lok Sabha in (2020)
o: the matter of creating new All India Services
questions.e: Constitution amendment bills must be passed by both houses separately. AIS is an exclusive power of RS; removal of govt is exclusive to LS.

questions.q: With reference to the funds under Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS), which of the following statements are correct? 1️⃣ MPLADS funds must be used to create durable assets like physical infrastructure for health, education, etc. 2️⃣ A specified portion of each MP's fund must benefit SC/ST populations. 3️⃣ MPLADS funds are sanctioned on yearly basis and the unused funds cannot be carried forward to the next year. 4️⃣ The district authority must inspect at least 10% of all works under implementation every year. (2020)
questions.e: MPLADS funds are non-lapsable (can be carried forward), making Statement 3 incorrect.

questions.q: Which one of the following categories of Fundamental Rights incorporates protection against untouchability as a form of discrimination? (2020)
questions.e: Article 17 (untouchability) falls under the "Right to Equality" (Articles 14-18).

questions.q: In India, separation of judiciary from the executive is enjoined by (2020)
o: a Directive Principle of State Policy
questions.e: Article 50 of the DPSPs directs the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in public services.

questions.q: 'The Macro Economic Framework Statement' is presented to Parliament mandated by (2020)
o: Article 112 and Article 110(1) of the Constitution of India
Provisions of the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003
Article 113 of the Constitution of India
questions.e: The FRBM Act 2003 requires the government to lay this statement along with the budget.

questions.q: A constitutional government by definition is a (2020)
questions.e: Constitutionalism means the government's power is legally limited.

questions.q: Other than the Fundamental Rights, which of the following parts of the Constitution of India reflect/reflects the principles and provisions of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948)? 1️⃣ Preamble 2️⃣ Directive Principles of State Policy 3️⃣ Fundamental Duties (2020)
questions.e: India's constitutional values closely mirror the human rights protected in the UDHR.

questions.q: In India, Legal Services Authorities provide free legal services to which of the following type of citizens? 1️⃣ Person with an annual income of less than 1,00,000 2️⃣ Transgender with an annual income of less than 2,00,000 3️⃣ Member of Other Backward Classes (OBC) with an annual income of less than ₹3,00,000 4️⃣ All Senior Citizens (2020)
questions.e: Senior citizens have varying income caps by state; not "all" are covered. OBCs are not a distinct category in NALSA rules unless they fit income/other criteria.

questions.q: A Parliamentary System of Government is one in which (2020)
o: the Government is chosen by the Parliament but cannot be removed by it before completion of a fixed term
the Government is responsible to the Parliament and can be removed by it
all political parties in the Parliament are represented in the Government
the Government is elected by the people and can be removed by them
questions.e: The Executive's accountability to the Legislature is the hallmark.

questions.q: Which part of the Constitution of India declares the ideal of Welfare State? (2020)
questions.e: Part IV aims at establishing social and economic democracy.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Constitution of India defines its 'basic structure' in terms of federalism, secularism, fundamental rights and democracy. 2️⃣ The Constitution of India provides for 'judicial review' to safeguard the citizens' liberties and to preserve the ideals on which the Constitution is based. (2020)
questions.e: The "basic structure" is a judicial innovation (Kesavananda Bharati), not defined in the text. Judicial review is provided through various Articles (13, 32, 226).

questions.q: One common agreement between Gandhism and Marxism is (2020)
o: the final goal of a stateless Society
questions.e: Both envisioned an ultimate stage of society where the state would no longer be necessary.

questions.q: In the context of India, which one of the following is the characteristic appropriate for bureaucracy? (2020)
o: An agency for widening the scope of parliamentary democracy
An agency for the implementation of public policy
An agency for facilitating political stability and economic growth
An agency for strengthening the structure of federalism
questions.e: Bureaucracy is the administrative machinery for executing laws and government programs.

questions.q: The Preamble to the Constitution of India is (2020)
o: a part of the Constitution and has the same legal effect as any other part
not a part of the Constitution and has no legal effect either
a part of the Constitution but has no legal effect
a part of the Constitution but has no legal effect independently of other parts
questions.e: It's a part (Kesavananda), but its provisions aren't independently enforceable; they aid in interpretation.

questions.q: With reference to the provisions contained in Part IV of the Constitution of India, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ They shall be enforceable by courts. 2️⃣ They shall not be enforceable by any court. 3️⃣ The principles laid down in this part are to influence the making of laws by the State. (2020)
questions.e: Articles 37 defines DPSPs as non-justiciable but fundamental to law-making.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ According to the Constitution of India, a person who is eligible to vote can be made a minister in a State for six months even if he/she is not a member of the Legislature of that State. 2️⃣ According to the Representation of People Act, 1951, a person convicted of a criminal offence and sentenced to imprisonment for five years is permanently disqualified from contesting an election even after his release from prison. (2020)
questions.e: Statement 1 is false because eligibility to be a minister usually requires 25 years (Assembly) or 30 (Council), while voting age is 18. Statement 2 is false as disqualification is usually for the sentence period plus 6 years.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The President of India can summon a session of the Parliament at such place as he/she thinks fit. 2️⃣ The Constitution of India provides for three, sessions of the Parliament in a year, but it is not mandatory to conduct all three sessions. 3️⃣ There is no minimum number of days that the Parliament is required to meet in a year. (2020)
questions.e: The Constitution doesn't mandate three sessions, only that the gap between two sessions mustn't exceed 6 months. There's no minimum-day requirement.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919 recommended granting voting rights to all the women above the age of 21. 2️⃣ The Government of India Act of 1935 gave women reserved seats in legislature. (2021)
questions.e: The 1919 Act allowed states to decide on women's suffrage (limited). The 1935 Act provided separate electorates for women.

questions.q: How does our model of parliamentary democracy differ from the British model? 1️⃣ As regards legislation, the British Parliament is supreme or sovereign but in India, the power of the Parliament to legislate is limited. 2️⃣ In India, matters related to the constitutionality of the Amendment of an Act of the Parliament are referred to the Constitution Bench by the Supreme Court. (2021)
questions.e: India has a written Constitution and judicial review, limiting Parliament. British Parliament is sovereign.

questions.q: With reference to the Union Government, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ N. Gopalaswamy lyengar Committee suggested that a minister and a secretary be designated solely for pursuing the subject of administrative reform and promoting it. 2️⃣ In 1970, the Department of Personnel was constituted on the recommendation of the Administrative Reforms Commission, 1966, and this was placed under the Prime Minister's charge. (2021)
questions.e: Iyengar suggested restructuring ministries, but the secretary-solely-for-reforms was an ARC idea. The DoP was created under PMO based on ARC.

questions.q: 'Right to Privacy' is protected under which Article of the Constitution of India? (2021)
questions.e: Article 21's expansive interpretation covers privacy.

questions.q: With reference to India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Judicial custody means an accused is in the custody of the concerned magistrate and such accused is locked up in police station, not in jail. 2️⃣ During judicial custody, the police officer in charge of the case is not allowed to interrogate the suspect without the approval of the court. (2021)
questions.e: Judicial custody means being in jail, not a police lock-up. Police need court permission for interrogation during this time.

questions.q: With reference to India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ When a prisoner makes out a sufficient case, parole cannot be denied to such prisoner because it becomes a matter of his/her right. 2️⃣ State Governments have their own Prisoners Release on Parole Rules. (2021)
questions.e: Parole is a privilege, not a right. Prison administration is a state subject, so rules vary by state.

questions.q: At the national level, which ministry is the nodal agency to ensure effective implementation of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006? (2021)
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
questions.e: MoTA is responsible for this Act's implementation.

questions.q: A legislation which confers on the exесиtive or administrative authority an unguided and uncontrolled discretionary power in the matter of application of law violates which one of the following Articles of the Constitution of India? (2021)
questions.e: Arbitrary discretion violates the principle of equality and rule of law under Article 14.

questions.q: Which one of the following in Indian polity is an essential feature that indicates that it is federal in character? (2021)
o: The Union Cabinet can have elected representatives from regional parties.
The Union Legislature has elected representatives from constituent units.
The independence of judiciary is safeguarded.
The Fundamental Rights are enforceable by Courts of Law.
questions.e: An independent judiciary is vital in a federation to resolve disputes between units and the center.

questions.q: Which one of the following best defines the term 'State'? (2021)
o: A community of persons permanently occupying a definite territory independent of external control and possessing an organized government
A number of persons who have been living in a definite territory for a very long time with their own culture, tradition and government
A politically organized people of a definite territory and possessing an authority to govern them, maintain law and order, protect their natural rights and safeguard their means of sustenance
A society permanently living in a definite territory with a central authority, an executive responsible to the central authority and an independent judiciary
questions.e: This definition includes the four essential elements: people, territory, government, and sovereignty.

questions.q: With reference to Indian judiciary, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Any retired judge of the Supreme Court of India can be called back to sit and act as a Supreme Court judge by the Chief Justice of India with prior permission of the President of India. 2️⃣ A High Court in India has the power to review its own judgement as the Supreme Court does. (2021)
questions.e: Article 128 allows for retired SC judges to be called back. HCs are courts of record and have inherent power to review their decisions.

questions.q: With reference to India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ There is only one citizenship and one domicile. 2️⃣ A citizen by birth only can become the Head of State. 3️⃣ A foreigner once granted the citizenship cannot be deprived of it under any circumstances. (2021)
questions.e: India has single citizenship. Naturalized citizens can also become Head of State (unlike USA). Citizenship can be deprived on grounds like fraud or disloyalty.

questions.q: Which one of the following factors constitutes the best safeguard of liberty in a liberal democracy? (2021)
questions.e: Separation of powers prevents the concentration of authority and protects individual freedom.

questions.q: Under the Indian Constitution, concentration of wealth violates (2021)
o: the Directive Principles of State Policy
questions.e: Article 39(c) directs the State to ensure the economic system doesn't result in wealth concentration.

questions.q: What is the position of the Right to Property in India? (2021)
o: Legal right available to citizens only
Neither Fundamental Right nor legal right
Legal right available to any person
Fundamental Right available to citizens only
questions.e: It's a constitutional legal right under Article 300A, applicable to all "persons."

questions.q: What was the exact constitutional status of India on 26th January, 1950? (2021)
o: A Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic
questions.e: "Socialist" and "Secular" were added later by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.

questions.q: Constitutional government means (2021)
o: a government whose Head enjoys nominal powers
a government limited by the terms of the Constitution
a representative government of a nation with federal structure
a government whose Head enjoys real powers
questions.e: Limited government is the core meaning of constitutionalism.

questions.q: Consider the following statements in respect of Bharat Ratna and Padma Awards: 1️⃣ Bharat Ratna and Padma Awards are titles under the Article 18(1) of the Constitution of India. 2️⃣ Padma Awards, which were instituted in the year 1954, were suspended only once. 3️⃣ The number of Bharat Ratna Awards is restricted to a maximum of five in a particular year. (2021)
questions.e: (Note: The answer key in the PDF marks 'd', but historically these are not considered "titles" prohibited by Art 18).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Pursuant to the report of H.N. Sanyal Committee, the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 was passed. 2️⃣ The Constitution of India empowers the Supreme Court and the High Courts to punish for contempt of themselves. 3️⃣ The Constitution of India defines Civil Contempt and Criminal Contempt. 4️⃣ In India, the Parliament is vested with the powers to make laws on Contempt of Court. (2022)
questions.e: The Constitution grants the power to punish (Articles 129, 215) but the 1971 Act (not Constitution) defines types of contempt.

questions.q: With reference to India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Government law officers and legal firms are recognised as advocates, but corporate lawyers and patent attorneys are excluded from recognition as advocates. 2️⃣ Bar Councils have the power to lay down the rules relating to legal education and recognition of law colleges. (2022)
questions.e: BCI regulates legal standards. Corporate lawyers are generally not recognized as practicing advocates under current rules.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ A bill amending the Constitution requires a prior recommendation of the President of India. 2️⃣ When a Constitution Amendment Bill is presented to the President of India, it is obligatory for the President of India to give his/her assent. 3️⃣ A Constitution Amendment Bill must be passed by both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha by a special majority and there is no provision for joint sitting. (2022)
questions.e: No prior recommendation is needed. The 24th Amendment made Presidential assent mandatory. No joint sitting is allowed for CA bills.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Constitution of India classifies the ministers into four ranks viz. Cabinet Minister, Minister of State with Independent Charge, Minister of State and Deputy Minister. 2️⃣ The total number of ministers in the Union Government, including the Prime Minister, shall not exceed 15 percent of the total number of members in the Lok Sabha. (2022)
questions.e: The 15% limit was added by the 91st Amendment. The Constitution doesn't specify ranks; they are based on parliamentary rules.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the exclusive power(s) of Lok Sabha? 1️⃣ To ratify the declaration of Emergency 2️⃣ To pass a motion of no-confidence against the Council of Ministers 3️⃣ To impeach the President of India (2022)
questions.e: Emergency ratification and impeachment require both houses. Only the Lok Sabha can pass a no-confidence motion.

questions.q: With reference to anti-defection law in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The law specifies that a nominated legislator cannot join any political party within six months of being appointed to the House. 2️⃣ The law does not provide any time-frame within which the presiding officer has to decide a defection case. (2022)
questions.e: Nominated members can join a party within 6 months; if they join after that, they are disqualified. No statutory deadline exists for the Speaker's decision.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Attorney General of India and Solicitor General of India are the only officers of the Government who are allowed to participate in the meetings of the Parliament of India. 2️⃣ According to the Constitution of India, the Attorney General of India submits his resignation when the Government which appointed him resigns. (2022)
questions.e: Only the AG has a constitutional right to attend sessions (not Solicitor General). The AG resigns by convention, not because of a specific constitutional mandate.

questions.q: With reference to the writs issued by the Courts in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Mandamus will not lie against a private organisation unless it is entrusted with a public duty. 2️⃣ Mandamus will not lie against a Company even though it may be a Government Company. 3️⃣ Any public minded person can be a petitioner to move the Court to obtain the writ of Quo Warranto. (2022)
questions.e: Mandamus can lie against a govt company. Quo Warranto can be sought by any person (not just the aggrieved).

questions.q: With reference to Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ As per the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha, the election of Deputy Speaker shall be held on such date as the Speaker may fix. 2️⃣ There is a mandatory provision that the election of a candidate as Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha shall be from either the principal opposition party or the ruling party. 3️⃣ The Deputy Speaker has the same power as of the Speaker when presiding over the sitting of the House and no appeal lies against his rulings. 4️⃣ The well established parliamentary practice regarding the appointment of Deputy Speaker is that the motion is moved by the Speaker and duly seconded by the Prime Minister. (2022)
questions.e: Statement 2 is a convention (opposition candidate), not a mandatory law. Statement 4 is false as the motion is moved by other members, not the Speaker.

questions.q: In the Government of India Act 1919, which of the following were treated as "Reserved" subjects? 1️⃣ Administration of Justice 2️⃣ Local Self-Government 3️⃣ Land Revenue 4️⃣ Police (2022)
questions.e: Local Self-Government was a "Transferred" subject.

questions.q: If a particular area is brought under the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution of India, which one of the following statements best reflects the consequence of it? (2022)
o: This would convert that area into a Union Territory.
This would create a local self-governing body in that area.
The State having such areas would be declared a Special Category State.
This would prevent the transfer of land of tribal people to non-tribal people.
questions.e: The 5th Schedule provides for the protection of tribal lands from alienation.

questions.q: In essence, what does 'Due Process of Law' mean? (2023)
questions.e: It implies that laws must be just, fair, and reasonable, incorporating natural justice.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Statement-I: In India, prisons are managed by State Governments with their own rules and regulations for the day-to-day administration of prisons. Statement-II: In India, prisons are governed by the Prisons Act, 1894 which expressly kept the subject of prisons in the control of Provincial Governments. (2023)
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-1 is incorrect but Statement- II is correct
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: Prison is a state subject. The 1894 Act provides the basic framework, leaving details to states.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the Chief purpose of the "Constitution" of a country? (2023)
o: It determines the objective for the making of necessary laws.
It enables the creation of political offices and a government.
It defines and limits the powers of government.
It secures social justice, social equality and social security.
questions.e: A constitution's primary legal role is to define the boundaries of state power.

questions.q: In India, which one of the following Constitutional Amendments was widely believed to be enacted to overcome the judicial interpretations of the Fundamental Rights? (2023)
questions.e: The 1st Amendment (1951) was brought in to address court rulings on land reforms and free speech.

questions.q: Consider the following organizations/ bodies in India: 1️⃣ The National Commission for Backward Classes 2️⃣ The National Human Rights Commission 3️⃣ The National Law Commission 4️⃣ The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. How many of the above are constitutional bodies? (2023)
questions.e: Only NCBC (Article 338B) is constitutional. NHRC and NCDRC are statutory; Law Commission is an executive body.

questions.q: How many of the following statements are correct? 1️⃣ If the election of the President of India is declared void by the Supreme Court of India, all acts done by him/her in the performance of duties before the date of decision become invalid. 2️⃣ Election for the post of the President of India can be postponed on the ground that some Legislative Assemblies have been dissolved. 3️⃣ When a Bill is presented to the President of India, the Constitution prescribes time limits within which he/she has to declare his/her assent. (2023)
questions.e: Acts remain valid. Dissolution of an assembly is not grounds for postponement. No time limit is fixed for presidential assent.

questions.q: How many of the following statements regarding Finance/Money Bills are correct? 1️⃣ When the Lok Sabha transmits Finance Bill to the Rajya Sabha, it can amend or reject the Bill. 2️⃣ When the Lok Sabha transmits Money Bill to the Rajya Sabha, it cannot amend or reject the Bill, it can only make recommendations. 3️⃣ In the case of disagreement between the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, there is no joint sitting for Money Bill, but a joint sitting becomes necessary for Finance Bill. (2023)
questions.e: Statement 1 is true for Finance Bill Type II. Statement 2 is true for Money Bills. Joint sitting is possible for Finance Bills but not Money Bills.

questions.q: How many of the following statements regarding 'Scheduled Areas' are correct? 1️⃣ Within a State, the notification of an area as Scheduled Area takes place through an Order of the President. 2️⃣ The largest administrative unit forming the Scheduled Area is the District and the lowest is the cluster of villages in the Block. 3️⃣ The Chief Ministers of the concerned States are required to submit annual reports to the Union Home Ministry on the administration of Scheduled Areas. (2023)
questions.e: Governors (not CMs) submit reports to the President.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Statement-I: The Supreme Court of India has held in some judgements that the reservation policies made under Article 16(4) would be limited by Article 335 for maintenance of efficiency of administration. Statement-II: Article 335 of the Constitution of India defines the term 'efficiency of administration'. (2023)
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-1
Statement-i is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-l is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-1 and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
questions.e: The SC has often balanced reservation with efficiency (Art 335), but "efficiency" is not defined in the Constitution.

questions.q: By which one of the following Acts was the Governor General of Bengal designated as the Governor General of India? (2023)
questions.e: Lord William Bentinck became the first GG of India under this Act.

questions.q: How many of the following statements are correct? 1️⃣ According to the Constitution of India, the Central Government has a duty to protect States from internal disturbances. 2️⃣ The Constitution of India exempts the States from providing legal counsel to a person being held for preventive detention. 3️⃣ According to the Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002, confession of the accused before the police cannot be used as evidence. (2023)
questions.e: Article 355 places the duty to protect states. Article 22(3) denies counsel rights for preventive detention. POTA (now repealed) actually allowed confessions to certain police officers as evidence.

questions.q: How many of the following statements in respect of election to the President of India are correct? 1️⃣ Nominated members of Parliament/Assemblies are eligible for the Electoral College. 2️⃣ Higher the number of elective Assembly seats, higher is the value of vote of each MLA. 3️⃣ The value of vote of each MLA of Madhya Pradesh is greater than that of Kerala. 4️⃣ The value of vote of each MLA of Puducherry is higher than that of Arunachal Pradesh. (2023)
questions.e: Only Statement 4 is correct based on the population-to-seat ratio. Nominated members cannot vote. MP and Kerala values are different but not in the way stated.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Statement-I: One of the standard sizes of the National Flag of India is 600 mm x 400 mm. Statement-II: The ratio of the length to the height (width) of the Flag shall be 3:2. (2023)
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: 600x400 is not a standard flag size (900x600 is). The ratio 3:2 is mandatory.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Statement-I: The Constitution Day is celebrated on 26th November every year. Statement-II: On 26th November, 1949, the Constituent Assembly set up a Drafting Committee under Dr. B. R. Ambedkar. (2023)
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-l is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: Constitution Day marks the adoption of the Constitution in 1949. The Drafting Committee was actually set up on 29th August 1947.

questions.q: How many of the following statements regarding Home Guards are correct? 1️⃣ Home Guards are raised under Central Government rules. 2️⃣ Their role is to serve as an auxiliary force to the police. 3️⃣ Border Wing Home Guards exist in some states to prevent infiltration. (2023)
questions.e: Home Guards are raised under state laws (State subject). Statements 2 and 3 are correct.

questions.q: How many of the following pairs are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Unauthorized uniforms : Official Secrets Act, 1923 2️⃣ Misleading a police officer : Evidence Act, 1872 3️⃣ Celebratory gunfire : Arms (Amendment) Act, 2019 (2023)
questions.e: Uniforms and misleading officers are covered under the OSA. Celebratory gunfire is an offense under the 2019 Arms Act amendment.

questions.q: A Writ of Prohibition is an order issued by the Supreme Court or High Courts to: (2024)
o: the Government prohibiting it from following an unconstitutional policy.
the Parliament/Legislative Assembly to pass a law on Prohibition.
the lower court prohibiting continuation of proceedings in a case.
a government officer prohibiting him from taking a particular action.
questions.e: Prohibition is issued to judicial or quasi-judicial bodies to prevent them from exceeding their jurisdiction.

questions.q: Who was the Provisional President of the Constituent Assembly before Dr. Rajendra Prasad took over? (2024)
questions.e: As the oldest member, Sinha was elected provisional president on 9 Dec 1946.

questions.q: The Constitution (71st Amendment) Act, 1992 included which of the following languages? 1️⃣ Konkani 2️⃣ Manipuri 3️⃣ Nepali 4️⃣ Maithili (2024)
questions.e: Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali (KMN) were added by the 71st Amendment. Maithili was added later (92nd Amendment).

questions.q: As per Article 368, the Parliament may amend the Constitution by way of: 1️⃣ Addition 2️⃣ Variation 3️⃣ Repeal (2024)
questions.e: Article 368 explicitly uses these three terms to define the power of amendment.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is the Governor of the State who recognizes and declares any community of that State as a Scheduled Tribe. 2️⃣ A community declared as a Scheduled Tribe in a State need not be so in another State. (2024)
questions.e: The President (not Governor) declares STs after consultation. ST status is state-specific.

questions.q: The North Eastern Council (NEC) comprises which of the following members? 1️⃣ Governor of the Constituent State 2️⃣ Chief Minister of the Constituent State 3️⃣ Three Members to be nominated by the President of India 4️⃣ The Home Minister of India (2024)
questions.e: The 2002 amendment included the Home Minister as the ex-officio Chairman.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam': 1️⃣ Provisions will come into effect from the 18th Lok Sabha. 2️⃣ This will be in force for 15 years after becoming an Act. 3️⃣ There are provisions for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes Women within the quota reserved for the Scheduled Castes. (2024)
questions.e: Implementation depends on delimitation after the census (not 18th LS). It has a sunset clause of 15 years.

questions.q: Under which Article of the Constitution of India, has the Supreme Court of India placed the Right to Privacy? (2024)
questions.e: Article 21's right to life and personal liberty includes privacy.

questions.q: With reference to the Parliament of India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Prorogation of a House by the President does not require the advice of the Council of Ministers. 2️⃣ Prorogation is generally done after adjournment sine die but can be done while in session. 3️⃣ Dissolution is done on the advice of the Council of Ministers except in exceptional circumstances. (2024)
questions.e: Prorogation is an executive act done on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

questions.q: While any resolution for the removal of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is under consideration 1️⃣ He/She shall not preside. 2️⃣ He/She shall not have the right to speak. 3️⃣ He/She shall not be entitled to vote on the resolution in the first instance. (2024)
questions.e: Under Article 96, the Speaker cannot preside but can speak and has a first-instance vote (but no casting vote).

questions.q: Which of the following statements are correct? 1️⃣ Powers of Municipalities are in Part IX A. 2️⃣ Emergency provisions are in Part XVIII. 3️⃣ Amendment provisions are in Part XX. (2024)
questions.e: These parts correctly correspond to their respective constitutional subjects.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the Ethics Committee in the Lok Sabha are correct? 1️⃣ Initially it was an ad-hoc Committee. 2️⃣ Only a Member can make a complaint. 3️⃣ It cannot take up sub-judice matters. (2024)
questions.e: Any person (not just MPs) can complain if it's forwarded by an MP.

questions.q: With reference to Union Budget, consider the following: 1️⃣ Finance Minister lays the Annual Financial Statement on behalf of the PM. 2️⃣ No demand for grant can be made except on the recommendation of the President. (2024)
questions.e: The AFS is laid on behalf of the President (Article 112). Presidential recommendation is mandatory for grants (Article 113).

questions.q: How many Delimitation Commissions have been constituted by the Government of India till December 2023? (2024)
questions.e: Commissions were set up in 1952, 1963, 1973, and 2002.

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct as per the Constitution of India? (2024)
o: Corporation tax is a State subject.
Inter-State migration is a State subject.
Inter-State quarantine is a Union subject.
Inter-State trade and commerce is a State subject.
questions.e: Inter-state quarantine, migration, and trade are all Union subjects (List I). Corporation tax is also a Union tax.
